chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated from Ḥumrān, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man said to his female slave, “You are to me like the back of my mother,” intending by that to please his wife. He said: “He may approach her, and there is nothing upon her nor upon him.”

key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: the formula of likening a woman to one's mother in ẓihār

ai.seo_question: Does pronouncing ẓihār over a female slave create the same legal ruling as it does over a wife?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who used the formula of ẓihār toward his female slave rather than his wife. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that this statement carries no legal consequence here, and he may approach her without any liability upon either of them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4840 - Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated from Humran who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who said to his female slave, "You are to me as the back of my mother," intending by this statement to please his wife.
Imam (as) replied: "He may approach her (the slave), and there is nothing upon her or upon him."
